draft.title: Take each song's base colour from its album cover
draft.context: `PlaybackState` decodes the album cover URL but nothing uses it. Every song's palette starts from `RGB.random`, so the lights have nothing to do with what's playing. Worse, the decoder requires a cover, so a local file or a podcast episode (no `album.images`) makes `getPlaybackState` fail on every poll. Issue #10 asks for a new setting, `light-show.album-cover-colours`, on by default. With it on, the song's palette is built from the most vivid colour covering at least about 5% of the cover. The lights wait at most 1 s for it, then fall back to a random palette for the whole song, and covers are remembered by URL.
draft.decision:
Split the work into a pure part and an I/O part. Show the base colour on `TrackShow`.

1. Pure (`domain.engine.CoverColour.base`): takes the cover's pixels. Pixels that aren't vivid (low saturation or brightness, i.e. black, white or grey) only count towards the total. The vivid ones are grouped into hue bins. Bins holding at least `MinShare = 0.05` of all pixels are candidates, and the result is the mean colour of the most vivid candidate bin, or None if there is none. `Palette.from(base, type)` builds any palette type from a given base, and `Palette.random` keeps its behaviour as `RGB.random.flatMap(from(_, type))`.
2. I/O (`client.AlbumCovers`): GETs the cover with the existing Spotify HTTP client (system trust store, follows redirects). It decodes the bytes with `javax.imageio.ImageIO` in `Sync.blocking`, downsamples to at most 64×64 pixels and runs `CoverColour.base`. Each successful result, including None, is kept in a `Ref[F, Map[String, Option[RGB]]]` by URL. Failures aren't cached, so a later track retries. Failures are raised as the sealed `CoverError`.
3. Engine: `showFor(trackId, cover)` runs the tempo lookup and the cover lookup with `parTupled`. The cover side is `covers.baseColour(url).timeoutTo(CoverWait = 1.second, raise TimedOut)`. Any `CoverError` or other failure logs one WARN and falls back to a random base. The show is built once per track, so a cover that arrives late is dropped (the timed-out fetch is cancelled) and the palette can't change mid-song. `TrackShow` gains `base: RGB`. `applyNow` rebuilds the palette with `Palette.from(show.base, newType)`, so the base is kept whether it came from the cover or was random. With the setting off, or with no cover URL, nothing is fetched and the base is `RGB.random(using random)`. That keeps today's palettes for a given seed.

`SyncEngine.make` takes `covers: Option[AlbumCovers[F]] = None`, resolved to `AlbumCovers.none[F]` inside the body. A default argument can't see the `Async` context bound, so it can't build `none[F]` itself. Existing call sites and tests don't change. One PR: the change is small, and the decoder fix, the setting and the engine only make sense together.

draft.contracts:
- Config key `light-show.album-cover-colours` (Boolean, default `true` in the case class and in `reference.conf`): additive. A missing key means on.
- Shared model `LightShowConfig` (`model`, JVM and JS): the new field `albumCoverColours` is appended last with a default, so it's additive for Scala callers. `ConfigSnippet` emits it as `album-cover-colours` only when it's false.
- Settings JSON (`GET/POST /api/settings` and the `SettingsView` it carries): every `LightShowConfig` object gains `"albumCoverColours": true|false`. The response is additive. The derived circe codec has no defaults, so a POST without the field is rejected. The page and the server ship together from one build, so nothing that's actually used breaks.
- `PlaybackState.albumCoverUrl`: `String` → `Option[String]`. This is not additive, but the type is internal: its only users are `SyncEngine` and `PlaybackStateSpec`, both updated. The decoder becomes more lenient: a missing album, missing images or an empty images array decodes to None.
- `TrackShow` gains `base: RGB`: internal, built only by `SyncEngine`.
- `SyncEngine.showFor(trackId, cover: Option[String] = None)` and `SyncEngine.make(…, covers: Option[AlbumCovers[F]] = None)`: additive (new defaulted parameters).
- Palette API `GET /api/palette` (`ShowControls.palette`): unchanged in shape. It returns the colours of the palette in use.
- Outbound HTTP: one new GET per new cover URL to Spotify's image CDN (`i.scdn.co`). It sends no credentials.
- No new environment variables.
draft.failureModes:
The error type is a sealed `client.CoverError extends RuntimeException`, with these cases: `Refused(url, status)` (non-2xx), `Unreachable(url, error)` (connection, TLS or DNS failure), `Unreadable(url)` (ImageIO returns null or throws, or the image has no pixels), `TimedOut(url, after)`.
- Cover fetch or read (AlbumCovers boundary): every case is recoverable. `showFor` recovers each one, and any other non-fatal throwable, into a random base and logs one WARN. Nothing is cached on failure, so the next track with that cover retries. A cover with no vivid colour is not an error: it gives `Right(None)`, which is cached, produces a random base and logs no WARN.
- 1 s wait (engine boundary): `timeoutTo` cancels the fetch and raises `TimedOut`. This is recoverable in the same way. The show is fixed for the track, so a late cover is never applied.
- Playback decoding: a missing cover is no longer a failure. Other decode failures stay as they are (logged as ERROR by the poller).
- Palette construction: `Palette.from` returns `Option`. None (never expected for a valid RGB) stays fatal for that show, raised as today's `IllegalStateException`.
- Startup: a non-boolean `album-cover-colours` is a pureconfig `ConfigReaderException`, and the app refuses to start, as it does for any other malformed key.
draft.config: `light-show.album-cover-colours = true` (Boolean). Default: `true`, from both `reference.conf` and the case-class default. Validation: pureconfig's Boolean reader rejects anything else at startup. It doesn't change `LightShowConfig.problems`, because any Boolean is valid. Like every light-show setting, it's editable on the settings page, held in `LiveSettings` and taken up at the next song start via `live.startSong`. The 1 s wait (`SyncEngine.CoverWait`), the 5% share (`CoverColour.MinShare`) and the downsample size are constants, not settings: the issue fixes them.
draft.observability:
- WARN, once per song, when the cover fails or times out. Message: "Couldn't take the colours from the album cover for <trackId>, using a random palette: <error message>". Structured fields: `track_id`, `cover_url`, `reason` (the `CoverError` case name: `refused` | `unreachable` | `unreadable` | `timed_out`), `status` (Refused only), `waited_ms` (TimedOut only).
- INFO: the existing "New show for <trackId>: pulsing at … palette <type>" line also says where the base came from: "base #rrggbb from the album cover" or "random base #rrggbb". There's no other log for a cover without a vivid colour, a song without a cover, or the setting being off.
- DEBUG in `AlbumCovers` when a cover is read: `cover_url`, `base` (hex or none), `pixels`. Nothing from `.env`, and no image bytes, is ever logged.
alternatives: Fetch the cover in the poller, or a background fiber, as soon as the playback state names a new URL, and let `showFor` read a `Deferred`. The renderer would never block, but this adds a fiber and shared state for a wait the issue already caps at 1 s. The tempo lookup already blocks the first frame the same way.

Let a timed-out fetch keep running under a `Supervisor` to warm the cache for the next track. Rejected for now: more lifecycle to manage, and the issue only requires cache hits after a successful read.

Run k-means or median-cut over the pixels instead of hue bins. It's harder to make deterministic and to test with tables, and the issue's rule (most vivid colour with a share of at least 5%) maps directly onto bins.

package domain.config

import domain.engine.PaletteType
import io.circe.Codec

/**
 * The light show's settings. `area` is the entertainment area to play on, by name; without one, the app uses
 * `hue.zone-id`, or the bridge's only music area. `albumCoverColours` builds each song's palette from its album cover's
 * colour rather than a random one.
 */
case class LightShowConfig(
  palette: PaletteType = PaletteType.Analogous,
  beatSource: BeatSource = BeatSource.Spotify,
  audio: AudioSettings = AudioSettings(),
  reactive: ReactiveSettings = ReactiveSettings(),
  defaultBpm: Double = 20.0,
  beatsPerPulse: Double = 1.0,
  syncOffsetMs: Long = -150,
  frameIntervalMs: Long = 16,
  pulse: PulseSettings = PulseSettings(),
  pause: PauseSettings = PauseSettings(),
  area: Option[String] = None,
  albumCoverColours: Boolean = true
) derives Codec.AsObject

object LightShowConfig {

  /** Everything that can't work in these settings, each naming the setting as the config file does; empty if none. */
  def problems(c: LightShowConfig): List[String] = {
    val p = c.pulse
    val swell = c.reactive.colourSwell
    List(
      Option.when(c.area.exists(_.trim.isEmpty))("area can't be empty"),
      Option.when(c.defaultBpm <= 0)("default-bpm must be positive"),
      Option.when(c.beatsPerPulse <= 0)("beats-per-pulse must be positive"),
      Option.when(c.frameIntervalMs <= 0)("frame-interval-ms must be positive"),
      Option.when(p.attack < 0 || p.sustain < 0)("pulse.attack and pulse.sustain can't be negative"),
      Option.when(p.attack + p.sustain >= 1)("pulse.attack + pulse.sustain must be less than 1"),
      Option.when(p.decayCurve <= 0)("pulse.decay-curve must be positive"),
      Option.when(p.restLevel < 0 || p.peakBoost < 0)("pulse.rest-level and pulse.peak-boost can't be negative"),
      Option.when(c.pause.fadeOutMs < 0)("pause.fade-out-ms can't be negative"),
      Option.when(c.audio.minBpm <= 0 || c.audio.maxBpm <= c.audio.minBpm)("audio.min-bpm must be positive and below audio.max-bpm"),
      Option.when(c.audio.device.trim.isEmpty)("audio.device can't be empty"),
      Option.when(c.audio.holdSeconds < 0)("audio.hold-seconds can't be negative"),
      Option.when(c.reactive.quietest <= 0 || c.reactive.loudest < c.reactive.quietest)(
        "reactive.quietest must be positive and no more than reactive.loudest"
      ),
      Option.when(c.reactive.flash < 0 || c.reactive.flash > 1 || c.reactive.sparkle < 0 || c.reactive.sparkle > 1)(
        "reactive.flash and reactive.sparkle must be between 0 and 1"
      ),
      Option.when(c.reactive.flashDecayMs <= 0 || c.reactive.sparkleDecayMs <= 0)(
        "reactive.flash-decay-ms and reactive.sparkle-decay-ms must be positive"
      ),
      Option.when(c.reactive.hitRatio <= 1 || c.reactive.sparkleRatio <= 1)("reactive.hit-ratio and reactive.sparkle-ratio must be above 1"),
      Option.when(c.reactive.roles.isEmpty)("reactive.roles needs at least one role"),
      Option.when(c.reactive.colourReach < 0)("reactive.colour-reach can't be negative"),
      Option.when(c.reactive.colourSwell.beats <= 0)("reactive.colour-swell.beats must be positive"),
      Option.when(swell.attack < 0 || swell.sustain < 0)("reactive.colour-swell.attack and reactive.colour-swell.sustain can't be negative"),
      Option.when(swell.attack + swell.sustain >= 1)("reactive.colour-swell.attack + reactive.colour-swell.sustain must be less than 1"),
      Option.when(swell.decayCurve <= 0)("reactive.colour-swell.decay-curve must be positive"),
      Option.when(swell.restLevel < 0 || swell.peakBoost < 0)(
        "reactive.colour-swell.rest-level and reactive.colour-swell.peak-boost can't be negative"
      )
    ).flatten
  }

  def validate(c: LightShowConfig): Either[String, LightShowConfig] =
    problems(c) match {
      case Nil => Right(c)
      case found => Left(found.mkString("; "))
    }
}

slices.title: Base colour from the album cover, with an optional cover and the album-cover-colours setting
slices.delivers: Songs whose cover has a vivid colour covering at least 5% of it get a palette built from that colour. Every other song, including one with no cover, a failed or slow cover, or the setting off, gets a random palette as today. Playback states without a cover no longer fail. The setting is on the settings page and covers are remembered by URL. Docs are updated.
acceptanceCriteria: A cover that is mostly vivid red gives a palette whose base colour has a red hue. A cover that is mostly vivid blue gives a blue base. The palette API returns that palette's colours in today's shape.

A cover that is all black, white and grey except for a vivid colour under 5% of it gives a random palette. A mostly grey cover with a vivid colour covering 5% or more gives a base with that colour's hue.

A cover that answers 404 or 500, can't be reached, or isn't an image still leaves the song playing with a random palette, and exactly one WARN (reason refused, unreachable or unreadable) is logged for that song.
A cover that takes longer than 1 s gives a random palette and one WARN with reason timed_out. The palette API returns the same colours for the rest of the song after the cover would have arrived.
A second track with the same cover URL starts with the cover-derived palette, and the cover server receives no second request.
A playback state whose item has no album, or has an empty images list, decodes without error. The song plays with a random palette, no cover request is made and no WARN is logged.
After "Apply now" with a different palette type mid-song, the palette is of the new type and built from the base the song started with, both for a cover-derived base and a random one.
With album-cover-colours off, no cover request is made and the palettes for a given seed equal today's.

With no light-show.album-cover-colours in the config, the app loads it as true. The settings page shows an "album-cover-colours" checkbox in the All lights section. Unticking it is saved as false, the next song fetches no cover, and the song playing at the time keeps its palette.

docs/how-it-works.md says the base colour is the most vivid colour covering about 5% or more of the album cover. It says the app waits at most 1 second for the cover, falls back to a random palette for the whole song when the cover is missing, slow, unreadable or has no vivid colour, remembers each cover by URL, and that light-show.album-cover-colours = false turns this off.
docs/roadmap.md no longer lists "Colours from the album cover". docs/architecture.md shows AlbumCovers between SyncEngine and the image CDN.

Plus ScalaCheck properties: the result is None whenever every pixel is neutral, and when the result is Some, at least 5% of the pixels share its hue bin. `PaletteSpec`: for every `PaletteType`, `Palette.from(base, t)` starts from `base`, and `random` with a seed equals `from(RGB.random(seed), t)`. `AlbumCoversSpec` (CatsEffectSuite): a fake http4s `Client.fromHttpApp` serves PNG bytes the test builds in memory, plus 404 and 500 responses, garbage bytes and a client that raises a connection error. It checks the `CoverError` case for each, and uses a request-counting `Ref` to show the cache hit. `PlaybackStateSpec`: tables of JSON with no album, empty images and images present. `SyncEngineCoverSpec`, under `TestControl` with a seeded `Random` and a fake Spotify over HTTP plus a fake `AlbumCovers`: covers a fast cover, a cover that sleeps 2 s (random palette, palette unchanged at 5 s), raised `CoverError`s, the setting off (the fake counts zero calls), the setting switched off via `live.update` and taking effect only at the next track, and `applyNow` with a new type keeping the base. WARNs are captured the way `SyncEngineLogSpec` does, and the test asserts exactly one per song. Config: loading a `ConfigSource.string` without the key gives `albumCoverColours == true`. findings.headline: A vivid colour split across two hue bins can miss the 5% rule and give a random palette
findings.ifIgnored: Real covers whose main colour sits on a bin edge (reds near 0°/360° especially) get random palettes, while synthetic test pixels still pass.
findings.problem: The rule groups vivid pixels into fixed hue bins and counts a bin only if it alone holds 5% of the cover. The design never says how wide a bin is, where the edges are, or how 'most vivid' and 'vivid' are measured. A colour covering 6% of a JPEG cover, with normal hue noise across an edge such as 355°–5°, can split into two bins of 3% each. Neither bin qualifies, so the song gets a random palette, which breaks criterion 3 for real covers. A bin that is too wide merges different colours into one muddy mean instead. The table tests use single exact hues, so they won't catch either problem.
findings.suggestion: Fix the bin count and the saturation and brightness thresholds as named constants. Count each bin's share together with its neighbours, or use bins that wrap around 0°/360° with a sliding window. Add a table case with a vivid patch just over 5% whose hues straddle a bin edge, including red around 0°.

findings.headline: Planned palette test asserts every palette type starts with the base colour, which is false
findings.ifIgnored: The PaletteSpec property fails as written, or gets weakened ad hoc while the slice is built, and the cover-colour tests have no defined way to find the base in a palette.
findings.problem: `RGB.analogous` is `List(rotateHue(-30), c, rotateHue(30))`, so the base is the middle colour. `monochromatic` maps the base through `withBrightness(0.35/0.65/1.0)`, so the base itself isn't in the palette unless its brightness is already 1.0. `AnalogousComplementary` likewise starts with a rotated colour. The property "for every PaletteType, Palette.from(base, t) starts from base" doesn't hold for these types. The tests for 'base colour is red' through the palette API (criteria 1 and 4) depend on the same false assumption, and the default type is Analogous.
findings.suggestion: Specify the property for each type, e.g. `from(base, t) == random(t)` with the RNG fixed to yield `base`, or define a 'base position' or hue check for each type. In the end-to-end tests, check the hue of the right palette entry, or check `TrackShow.base`, and keep the palette API check to its shape.

findings.headline: The 1-second wait can run over while an image is still being decoded
findings.ifIgnored: A large or slow-to-decode cover can hold the renderer past 1 s at song start; this is rare with Spotify's 640px JPEGs.
findings.problem: Image decoding runs in `Sync.blocking`, which can't be cancelled. The design calls `timeoutTo(CoverWait, …)` on the whole cover lookup. If the timeout fires during the decode, cancelling waits for `ImageIO.read` to finish. The claim that the lights 'wait at most 1 second' then doesn't strictly hold, and the frame loop stalls until the decode ends.
findings.suggestion: Use `Sync.interruptible` for the decode, or race the fetch with `Concurrent.race`/`start` and drop the losing fiber without waiting on it. Or state the bound as 1 s plus the decode time.

findings.headline: No single test covers a failed cover fetch over HTTP through to exactly one WARN
findings.ifIgnored: Cover fetch failures are mapped to errors in one test and counted as WARNs in another, so a wiring gap between the two (e.g. a non-CoverError escaping) goes unnoticed.
findings.problem: Criterion 5 is about real fetch failures (an error response, an unreachable host, bytes that aren't an image). AlbumCoversSpec tests those over HTTP, but SyncEngineCoverSpec counts WARNs with a fake `AlbumCovers` that raises `CoverError` directly. CLAUDE.md says external services are faked over HTTP. A failure that the real `fromHttp` raises differently, such as a decode exception that isn't wrapped, is never pushed through the engine's recovery and WARN count.
findings.suggestion: In the engine spec, add at least one case that builds `AlbumCovers.fromHttp` on a `Client.fromHttpApp` returning 500 or garbage bytes, and assert exactly one WARN and a random palette.

draft.title: Take each song's base colour from its album cover
draft.context: `PlaybackState` decodes the album cover URL, but nothing uses it. Every song's palette starts from `RGB.random`. The decoder also requires a cover, so a local file or an episode without `album.images` makes every poll fail. Issue #10 adds `light-show.album-cover-colours`, on by default. When it's on, a song's palette is built from the most vivid colour that covers about 5% or more of the cover. The lights wait at most 1 s for that colour, use a random palette for the whole song otherwise, and remember each cover's colour by URL.
draft.decision:
One PR, split into a pure part and an I/O part. `TrackShow` records the base colour.

1. **Pure rule (`CoverColour.base`)**, using named constants. A pixel is *vivid* when its HSB saturation ≥ `MinSaturation = 0.35` and its brightness ≥ `MinBrightness = 0.25`. All other pixels (black, white, grey, muddy) count only towards the total. A pixel's *vividness* is saturation × brightness. Vivid pixels go into `HueBins = 36` bins of 10° each, where bin k covers [10k°, 10k+10°). For each bin k, a *window* is bins k−1, k and k+1, with indices taken mod 36, so it wraps through 0°/360°. A window qualifies when its pixels make up at least `MinShare = 0.05` of all pixels. Among qualifying windows, the one with the highest mean vividness wins, with a larger share breaking ties. The result is that window's circular-mean hue, with the mean saturation and brightness, built through `Hsb.toRgb`. None means no window qualifies. A 6% red patch whose noise spans bins 35 and 0 still qualifies through the window centred on bin 0. A window is only 30° wide, so distinct hues aren't averaged into mud.
2. **`Palette.from(base, type)`** builds every type from a given base. `random(t)` becomes `RGB.random.flatMap(from(_, t))`, so palettes for a given seed don't change.
3. **I/O (`AlbumCovers.fromHttp`)**: GET the cover with the existing Spotify client. Decode in `Sync.interruptible` (`ImageIO.read`), downsample to at most 64×64, then run `CoverColour.base`. Results, including None, are cached in a `Ref[Map[url, Option[RGB]]]`. Failures aren't cached. Errors are `CoverError`.
4. **Engine**: `showFor(trackId, cover)` runs the tempo lookup and `coverBase` with `parTupled`. `coverBase` *starts* the lookup as a fiber and waits on its join with `timeoutTo(CoverWait = 1.s)`. On timeout it cancels the fiber in the background (`fiber.cancel.start`) and doesn't wait for it, so the frame loop never waits more than 1 s, even mid-decode. A timeout or any failure logs one WARN and gives a random base. The show is fixed per track, so a cover that arrives late never changes it. `applyNow` builds the new type with `Palette.from(show.base, t)`. With the setting off or no URL, the base is `RGB.random(using random)`, exactly as today.

`make` takes `covers: Option[AlbumCovers[F]] = None` and resolves `AlbumCovers.none[F]` in the body. A default argument can't see the `Async` bound, which is what broke the last skeleton.

- `LightShowConfig` (shared model, JVM and JS): new field appended last with a default, so additive. `ConfigSnippet` emits `album-cover-colours = false` only when the value differs from the default.

draft.failureModes:
Errors are the sealed `client.CoverError extends RuntimeException`: `Refused(url, status)`, `Unreachable(url, error)`, `Unreadable(url)` (ImageIO returns null or throws, or there are no pixels) and `TimedOut(url, after)`. `fromHttp` maps every failure it meets into one of these, so nothing escapes unwrapped.
- **Fetch or read (AlbumCovers)**: all recoverable. `coverBase` recovers any `CoverError`, or any other non-fatal throwable, into a random base with one WARN. Failures aren't cached, so a later track retries.

- **1 s wait (engine)**: on timeout, `TimedOut` is recovered the same way. A read that finishes regardless may land in the cache, which only helps the next track. The current show never changes.
- **No cover / setting off**: nothing is fetched, the base is random and nothing is logged.
- **Playback decode**: a missing cover is no longer an error. Other decode failures are logged as ERROR, as today.
- **Startup**: a non-boolean value is a pureconfig failure, and the app refuses to start.
draft.config: `light-show.album-cover-colours = true` (Boolean), the default in both `reference.conf` and the case class. pureconfig's Boolean reader rejects anything else at startup. `LightShowConfig.problems` is unchanged, since every Boolean is valid. These are constants, not settings, because the issue fixes them: `SyncEngine.CoverWait = 1.second`, and in `CoverColour`, `MinShare = 0.05`, `MinSaturation = 0.35`, `MinBrightness = 0.25`, `HueBins = 36` and `WindowBins = 1` (neighbours on each side). `AlbumCovers.MaxSide = 64`.

import scala.util.Random
import settings.LiveSettings

/**
 * The track's tempo from Spotify, if it gave one, and the palette, settings and lights the show plays it with. `base` is
 * the colour the palette was built from, so a new palette type keeps it.
 */
case class TrackShow(tempo: Option[Double], palette: Palette, settings: LightShowConfig, zone: Zone, base: RGB) {
  def bpm: Double = tempo.getOrElse(settings.defaultBpm) / settings.beatsPerPulse
}

class SyncEngine[F[_]: Async] private (
  config: AppConfig,
  live: LiveSettings[F],
  zone: Zone,
  spotify: SpotifyClient[F],
  lights: Lights[F],
  current: Ref[F, Option[(TrackId, TrackShow)]],
  random: Random,
  audio: Stream[F, AudioReading],
  covers: AlbumCovers[F]
):

  private val logger: SelfAwareStructuredLogger[F] = Slf4jLogger.getLogger[F]

  private def randomBase: F[RGB] = ???

  private def paletteFrom(base: RGB, paletteType: PaletteType): F[Palette] = ???

  /**
   * The base colour from the song's album cover, if the settings take it from there and it's read within
   * `SyncEngine.CoverWait`. None otherwise, logging one warning if the cover couldn't be fetched or read in time. The
   * lookup runs on its own fiber, which is cancelled without waiting for it once the time is up.
   */
  private def coverBase(trackId: TrackId, cover: Option[String], settings: LightShowConfig): F[Option[RGB]] = ???

  /** The lights to play `settings` on: the area they name, or else the ones `before` played on (or the first zone). */
  private def zoneFor(settings: LightShowConfig, before: Option[TrackShow]): F[Zone] = {
    val fallback = before.fold(zone)(_.zone)
    settings.area match {
      case None => Async[F].pure(fallback)
      case Some(name) if before.exists(_.settings.area.contains(name)) => Async[F].pure(fallback)
      case Some(name) =>
        lights.zone(name).attempt.flatMap {
          case Right(Some(found)) => logger.info(s"Playing on the $name area").as(found)
          case Right(None) => logger.warn(s"There's no $name area on the bridge; staying where the show is").as(fallback)
          case Left(err) => logger.warn(s"Couldn't read the $name area from the bridge, staying where the show is: $err").as(fallback)
        }
    }
  }

  /**
   * The show for a track. A new track takes up the latest settings, its area's lights and a new palette, built from its
   * album cover's colour when there is one; the show then stays the same until the track changes, so changes from the
   * settings page wait for the next song.
   */
  def showFor(trackId: TrackId, cover: Option[String] = None): F[TrackShow] = ???

  /** The palette of the song playing now, if one has started. */
  def palette: F[Option[Palette]] = current.get.map(_.map(_._2.palette))

  /**
   * Takes up the latest settings now rather than at the next song, moving to another area if they name one. The palette
   * only changes if its type did, and is then built from the song's base colour.
   */
  def applyNow: F[Unit] = ???

  /**
   * Keeps `audioRef` up to date with what the music is doing, logging when the beat locks on, is lost or changes
   * tempo. On failure it clears the reading, so the show carries on with Spotify timing and no audio effects.
   */
  private def followAudio(audioRef: Ref[F, Option[AudioReading]]): Stream[F, Nothing] =
    audio
      .evalMapAccumulate(Option.empty[Double]) { (logged, reading) =>
        val (remembered, news) = SyncEngine.beatNews(logged, reading.beat)
        (news.traverse_(logger.info(_)) *> audioRef.set(Some(reading))).as((remembered, ()))
      }
      .drain
      .handleErrorWith { err =>
        Stream.exec(audioRef.set(None) *> logger.warn(s"Listening stopped, using Spotify timing instead: ${err.getMessage}"))
      }

  def run: Stream[F, Frame] =
    Stream.eval((SignallingRef[F, Option[LocalPlayback]](None), Ref.of[F, Option[AudioReading]](None)).tupled).flatMap { (stateRef, audioRef) =>
      val poller = Stream.awakeEvery[F](config.pollingIntervalMs.millis)
        .evalMap { _ =>
          spotify.getPlaybackState.handleErrorWith { err =>
            logger.error(s"Spotify Poll Failed: $err") *> Async[F].pure(None)
          }
        }
        .evalMap(state => Clock[F].realTimeInstant.map(now => state.map(LocalPlayback(_, now))))
        .evalMap(stateRef.set)

      val renderer = Stream.awakeEvery[F](config.lightShow.frameIntervalMs.millis)
        .evalMap(_ => stateRef.get)
        .evalMapAccumulate(Renderer.initial) { (rendered, playback) =>
          playback.filter(_.state.isPlaying) match {
            case Some(local) => playingFrame(local, audioRef).map(Renderer.playing)
            case None =>
              (Clock[F].monotonic, live.applied, current.get).mapN { (now, show, playing) =>
                Renderer.paused(rendered, now, playing.fold(zone)(_._2.zone), show.pause)
              }
          }
        }
        .map(_._2)

      renderer.merge(poller.drain).merge(followAudio(audioRef))
        .zipWithIndex
        .map((frame, i) => frame.copy(sequence = (i % 256).toInt))
    }

  /**
   * The frame for the current moment of a playing track. With a live beat, pulses follow it; otherwise they follow
   * Spotify's playback position at the track's tempo. With live audio, the effects follow the music too.
   */
  private def playingFrame(local: LocalPlayback, audioRef: Ref[F, Option[AudioReading]]): F[Frame] =
    for {
      track <- showFor(local.state.trackId, local.state.albumCoverUrl)
      show = track.settings
      reading <- audioRef.get
      monotonic <- Clock[F].monotonic
      now <- Clock[F].realTimeInstant
      heardAt = monotonic + show.audio.offsetMs.millis
      pulses = reading.flatMap(_.beat) match {
        case Some(b) => b.beatsAt(heardAt) / show.beatsPerPulse
        case None =>
          val latencyMs = java.time.Duration.between(local.receivedAt, now).toMillis
          SyncEngine.pulsesAt(local.state.progress.toMillis + latencyMs + show.syncOffsetMs, track.bpm)
      }
      effects = reading
        .filter(_ => show.reactive.enabled)
        .fold(Effects.neutral)(r => Effects.at(heardAt, r, track.zone.channels.size, show.reactive))
    } yield SyncEngine.pulseFrame(track.zone, track.palette, pulses, show.pulse, effects)

    spotify: SpotifyClient[F],
    zone: Zone,
    lights: Lights[F],
    random: Random = new Random(),
    audio: Stream[F, AudioReading] = Stream.empty,
    covers: Option[AlbumCovers[F]] = None
  ): F[SyncEngine[F]] = ???

  /** How long a song's start waits for its album cover before playing a random palette. */
  val CoverWait: FiniteDuration = 1.second

  /** How far the tempo has to move from the last one logged before it's logged again. */
  private val TempoChangeToLog: Double = 0.03

  /**
   * What to log about the beat, given the tempo logged last and the latest beat: that it locked on, that it was lost,
   * or that the tempo moved by more than `TempoChangeToLog`. Returns the tempo to remember and the message, if any.
   */
  def beatNews(logged: Option[Double], beat: Option[BeatState]): (Option[Double], Option[String]) =
    (logged, beat) match {
      case (None, Some(b)) => (Some(b.bpm), Some(f"Locked onto the beat at ${b.bpm}%.1f BPM (confidence ${b.confidence}%.1f)"))
      case (Some(_), None) => (None, Some("Lost the beat; using Spotify timing until it's back"))
      case (Some(was), Some(b)) if math.abs(b.bpm - was) / was > TempoChangeToLog =>
        (Some(b.bpm), Some(f"Tempo changed from $was%.1f to ${b.bpm}%.1f BPM (confidence ${b.confidence}%.1f)"))
      case _ => (logged, None)
    }

  /** Pulses elapsed at a playback position, pulsing at `bpm`. */
  def pulsesAt(positionMs: Long, bpm: Double): Double = positionMs * bpm / 60000.0

  private val White: RGB = RGB.safe(255, 255, 255).get

  /**
   * One frame of the show for every channel in the zone, `pulses` pulses into the music. Light i takes palette colour
   * i, and what it does depends on its role:
   *  - a pulse light peaks `stagger` of a pulse after light i - 1 (light 0 on every whole pulse), so the pulse travels
   *    across the zone, and its hue turns with the treble;
   *  - a rhythm light pulses with the bar's kick pattern, or on every pulse until there's a live beat;
   *  - a colour light swells once every `swell.beats` beats, peaking on the beat, and moves along the palette as the
   *    music goes higher or lower.
   * The effects scale the brightness and push lights towards white for flashes and sparkles.
   */
  def pulseFrame(zone: Zone, palette: Palette, pulses: Double, settings: PulseSettings, effects: Effects = Effects.neutral): Frame = {
    val updates = zone.channels.zipWithIndex.map { (channel, i) =>
      val (brightness, colour) = effects.roleOf(i) match {
        case LightRole.Pulse =>
          val own = palette.getColor(i)
          val level = Pulse.onBeat(pulses - i * settings.stagger, settings)
          (Pulse.brightness(level, settings, effects.intensity), if (effects.hueShift == 0) own else own.rotateHue(effects.hueShift))
        case LightRole.Rhythm =>
          val level = effects.rhythm.fold(Pulse.onBeat(pulses, settings))(r => Pulse.rhythm(r.groove, r.beats, settings))
          (Pulse.brightness(level, settings, effects.intensity), palette.getColor(i))
        case LightRole.Colour =>
          // Counted along the beat grid when there's a live beat, so every other beat stays the same beat as the tracker re-estimates.
          val beats = effects.rhythm.fold(pulses)(_.beats)
          val shape = effects.swell.shape
          (Pulse.brightness(Pulse.onBeat(beats / effects.swell.beats, shape), shape, effects.intensity), palette.along(i, effects.paletteShift))
      }
      val lit = colour.scaleBrightness(brightness)
      val white = effects.whiteFor(i)
      LightUpdate(channel, if (white <= 0) lit else lit.mix(White, white))
    }
    Frame(zone.id, updates)
  }

object LightShowConfig {

  /** Everything that can't work in these settings, each naming the setting as the config file does; empty if none. */
  def problems(c: LightShowConfig): List[String] = {
    val p = c.pulse
    val swell = c.reactive.colourSwell
    List(
      Option.when(c.area.exists(_.trim.isEmpty))("area can't be empty"),
      Option.when(c.defaultBpm <= 0)("default-bpm must be positive"),
      Option.when(c.beatsPerPulse <= 0)("beats-per-pulse must be positive"),
      Option.when(c.frameIntervalMs <= 0)("frame-interval-ms must be positive"),
      Option.when(p.attack < 0 || p.sustain < 0)("pulse.attack and pulse.sustain can't be negative"),
      Option.when(p.attack + p.sustain >= 1)("pulse.attack + pulse.sustain must be less than 1"),
      Option.when(p.decayCurve <= 0)("pulse.decay-curve must be positive"),
      Option.when(p.restLevel < 0 || p.peakBoost < 0)("pulse.rest-level and pulse.peak-boost can't be negative"),
      Option.when(c.pause.fadeOutMs < 0)("pause.fade-out-ms can't be negative"),
      Option.when(c.audio.minBpm <= 0 || c.audio.maxBpm <= c.audio.minBpm)("audio.min-bpm must be positive and below audio.max-bpm"),
      Option.when(c.audio.device.trim.isEmpty)("audio.device can't be empty"),
      Option.when(c.audio.holdSeconds < 0)("audio.hold-seconds can't be negative"),
      Option.when(c.reactive.quietest <= 0 || c.reactive.loudest < c.reactive.quietest)(
        "reactive.quietest must be positive and no more than reactive.loudest"
      ),
      Option.when(c.reactive.flash < 0 || c.reactive.flash > 1 || c.reactive.sparkle < 0 || c.reactive.sparkle > 1)(
        "reactive.flash and reactive.sparkle must be between 0 and 1"
      ),
      Option.when(c.reactive.flashDecayMs <= 0 || c.reactive.sparkleDecayMs <= 0)(
        "reactive.flash-decay-ms and reactive.sparkle-decay-ms must be positive"
      ),
      Option.when(c.reactive.hitRatio <= 1 || c.reactive.sparkleRatio <= 1)("reactive.hit-ratio and reactive.sparkle-ratio must be above 1"),
      Option.when(c.reactive.roles.isEmpty)("reactive.roles needs at least one role"),
      Option.when(c.reactive.colourReach < 0)("reactive.colour-reach can't be negative"),
      Option.when(c.reactive.colourSwell.beats <= 0)("reactive.colour-swell.beats must be positive"),
      Option.when(swell.attack < 0 || swell.sustain < 0)("reactive.colour-swell.attack and reactive.colour-swell.sustain can't be negative"),
      Option.when(swell.attack + swell.sustain >= 1)("reactive.colour-swell.attack + reactive.colour-swell.sustain must be less than 1"),
      Option.when(swell.decayCurve <= 0)("reactive.colour-swell.decay-curve must be positive"),
      Option.when(swell.restLevel < 0 || swell.peakBoost < 0)(
        "reactive.colour-swell.rest-level and reactive.colour-swell.peak-boost can't be negative"
      )
    ).flatten
  }

  def validate(c: LightShowConfig): Either[String, LightShowConfig] =
    problems(c) match {
      case Nil => Right(c)
      case found => Left(found.mkString("; "))
    }
}

slices.title: Base colour from the album cover, with an optional cover and the album-cover-colours setting
slices.delivers: Songs whose cover has a vivid colour covering at least 5% of it get a palette built from that colour. Every other song gets a random palette as today: no cover, a failed or slow cover, or the setting off. A playback state without a cover no longer fails. The setting is on the settings page, covers are remembered by URL, and the docs are updated.
acceptanceCriteria: A song whose cover is mostly vivid red (hue near 0°, including pixels at 355° and 5°) gets a `TrackShow.base` with a red hue. A song whose cover is mostly vivid blue gets a blue base. Each palette entry sits at the place its type puts the base (for Analogous, the middle entry has the base's hue).
`GET /api/palette` returns that show's colours in today's shape.

A cover that is black, white and grey apart from a vivid patch under 5% gives a random base. A mostly grey cover with a vivid patch just over 5% gives a base with that patch's hue, even when the patch's hues lie across a bin edge, including red across 0°/360°.
A cover that answers 500, can't be reached, or returns bytes that aren't an image leaves the song playing with a random base. Exactly one WARN is logged for that song.

A cover that takes 2 s gives a random base and one WARN with reason timed_out. The show's palette is the same at 5 s as at the song's start, and the first frame arrives within 1 s of the song starting.
A second track with the same cover URL gets the cover-derived base, and the cover server receives only one request.
A playback state with no album, or with an empty images list, decodes without error. The song plays with a random base, no cover request is made and no WARN is logged.
After "Apply now" with a different palette type mid-song, the palette equals `Palette.from(base, newType)` for the base the song started with, both for a cover-derived base and for a random one.
With album-cover-colours off, no cover request is made, and for a given seed the palettes equal what today's code produces.

With no light-show.album-cover-colours in the config, the setting loads as true. The settings page's All lights section shows an album-cover-colours checkbox after the palette choice. Unticking it saves false, the next song fetches no cover, and the song playing at the time keeps its palette.

docs/how-it-works.md says the base colour is the most vivid colour covering about 5% or more of the album cover, that black, white and grey don't count, and that the app waits at most 1 second for the cover. It says a random palette is used for the whole song when the cover is missing, slow, unreadable or has no vivid colour, that covers are remembered by URL, and that light-show.album-cover-colours = false turns this off.
docs/roadmap.md no longer lists "Colours from the album cover". docs/architecture.md shows AlbumCovers between SyncEngine and the image CDN.
slices.testStrategy:
`CoverColourSpec` table of synthetic pixel vectors: mostly red, mostly blue, all neutral, neutral plus 4% vivid, neutral plus 6% vivid, and a 6% red patch split between 356° and 4°. A 6% patch split between the bin edge at 30° (hues 28° and 32°) gives a base within 10° of 30°. Two separate 10% patches at 0° and 120° give one of those hues, not a blend. Properties: every pixel neutral gives None. A Some result's hue window holds at least `MinShare` of the pixels. Rotating every pixel's hue by a multiple of 10° rotates the base by the same amount.

`PaletteSpec` properties: with a fixed seed, `random(t)(using new Random(s)) == RGB.random(using new Random(s)).flatMap(from(_, t))` for every `PaletteType`. A table gives each type the place it puts the base: Complementary, Triadic and Tetradic at index 0; Analogous at index 1; Monochromatic has every entry at the base's hue and saturation with brightnesses 0.35, 0.65 and 1.0; AnalogousComplementary(Flat) at index 1; Interspersed at index 2.

`AlbumCoversSpec` (CatsEffectSuite): `Client.fromHttpApp` serves PNGs built in memory, plus 404, 500, garbage bytes and a raised `ConnectException`. It asserts each `CoverError` case, and a request-counting `Ref` shows the cache hit and that failures aren't cached.

`PlaybackStateSpec` table: no album, empty images, images present.

findings.headline: The test the design points to for counting WARNs doesn't capture logs
findings.ifIgnored: The "exactly one WARN per song" criteria (5, 6, 8) end up either untested or counting the wrong log lines.
findings.problem: The plan says WARN counts are "captured as `SyncEngineLogSpec` does". That spec only checks the pure `beatNews` message and never captures a log. The real helper is `testkit/Tls.capturedLogs`, a logback ListAppender on the root logger. Because it sits on the root logger, it also sees the parallel tempo lookup's "Couldn't fetch the tempo" WARN and any other WARN, so a plain count is fragile unless the fake Spotify always serves a tempo.
findings.suggestion: Name `Tls.capturedLogs` (or the ListAppender pattern in `SpotifyTokenFileSpec`) as the way to capture logs. Count only WARN events from the SyncEngine logger whose message is the album-cover warning. Have the fake Spotify answer audio-features successfully in the cover tests.

findings.headline: Hue-rotation property can't hold exactly on 8-bit colours, so it may fail at random
findings.ifIgnored: CoverColourSpec may fail now and then in CI on generated pixels near a bin edge or the 5% threshold.
findings.problem: "Rotating every pixel's hue by a multiple of 10° rotates the base by the same amount" is run over generated pixels. `RGB.rotateHue` goes back through 8-bit channels, so a rotated pixel's hue moves by slightly more or less than 10°. A pixel close to a bin edge can then land in the next bin, which changes window shares and can push a window across `MinShare`, or change which window wins. Even when the same window wins, the base's hue only matches to within rounding.
findings.suggestion: Build the generated pixels from hues kept away from bin edges, with patch shares kept clear of 5%, and compare the rotated base's hue within a tolerance (a degree or two), not for exact equality.

findings.headline: Covers are decoded at full size with no byte limit, and the decode can't be interrupted
findings.ifIgnored: A cover the CDN serves at an unusually large size could use a lot of memory, and a timed-out decode keeps a blocking thread busy until it finishes.
findings.problem: The design says the timed-out fiber's "interruptible decode stops at its next interrupt check". `ImageIO.read` generally ignores thread interrupts and runs to the end. The whole response body is read into memory and decoded at full resolution before being scaled down to 64×64, and nothing limits the body's size. Spotify's covers are about 640 px, so the risk is low, but the design's claim about cancelling isn't what will happen.
findings.suggestion: Say plainly that a cancelled decode finishes in the background and its result is thrown away. Cap the body read (e.g. a few MB) and treat anything larger as `Unreadable`. Optionally use an ImageReader with subsampling so the cover is decoded smaller to begin with.

resultJson.title: Add design for taking each song's base colour from its album cover
resultJson.body:
Design for LorenzoPrinsloo/spotify-hue-sync#10. This PR doesn't close the issue. It adds the design only, as skeleton code with `???` bodies, and the feature is not implemented here.

The design adds a `light-show.album-cover-colours` setting, on by default. When it's on, a song's palette is built from the most vivid colour covering about 5% or more of the album cover. The lights wait at most 1 s for it, then use a random palette for the whole song. Covers are cached by URL. It also makes `PlaybackState.albumCoverUrl` an `Option`, so a local file or episode with no cover no longer fails every poll.

Things to check in review:
- The design went through one critique and revision. The revision changed the colour rule to hue bins with a window of neighbouring bins that wraps round 0°/360°. It also made the cover lookup run on its own fiber, so a slow decode can't hold the renderer past 1 s.
- The critique found that the planned `PaletteSpec` property "every palette type starts with the base" is false for some types, such as Analogous. The test strategy was not corrected in the part of the design I could see, so check it before the tests are written.
- `.orca/runs/e27fac626ddf.progress.json` is the design run's progress record.
